item.title: My Headcanon In-Universe Explanation
item.content:encoded:
The thing about the Chaos Insurgency is that they began as a rogue SCP Foundation splinter cell. They now use the Foundation's usual methods in the pursuit of their own agenda.

And that's is all that every portrayal of the Chaos Insurgency has in common. At this point, I don't think it is possible to establish a definitive portrayal of this Group of Interest.

As such, I have come up with an in-universe explanation for this discrepancy. The Chaos Insurgency is actually a broad term for multiple renegade splinter organizations of the Foundation. There is no single Chaos Insurgency. In reality, there are multiple Chaos Insurgencies, each with their own goals and reasons for going against the Foundation.

item.content:encoded:
I really don't want to be snarky, but I didn't get the context of the quote at first either (I was absent for a lot of the planning but loved what chubert and TG came up with). So…I Googled it. It's a quote from Paradise Lost, where the silver-tongued devil Belial is attempting to persuade Satan to not pursue direct warfare with God:

What if the breath that kindled those grim fires,
Awaked, should blow them into sevenfold rage,
And plunge us in the flames; or from above
Should intermitted vengeance arm again
His red right hand to plague us?

Basically, if we go to war against Heaven, God's gonna kick our asses all the way back to Hell. (By the way, some scholars interpret the "red right hand" of God to be Jesus Christ. An interesting interpretation, seeing as how the CI believes it is the salvation of the world).

Belial convinces Satan to not go to war, but instead incite rebellion in Adam and Eve against God. Not force, but cunning. Not all out war, but almost like an insurgency of some sort…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Talked a lot with chubert, and I'm really excited for the future of this hub and this concept of the Chaos Insurgency.

I do agree that my main issue with this is that it didn't take enough of the good stuff that others came up with. I mean…

Let me just state this for the record: Slate Thunder is a hugely flawed piece. But Slate Thunder was brilliant conceptually, pulling together and stating explicitly things we'd always wanted to see but never got to see. The O5s splitting. The Foundation Civil War. The Insurgency and the Foundation being entangled, willingly and unwillingly, forever.

(And yeah, I'm sorry, the CI wiki… run by people who were banned from here for being 13 and/or people who can't write to our wiki's standards… that's not a good wiki, and we don't have anything to do with it on an official basis besides making them fix their licensing errors. Sorry.)

I think the rest of this is really cool. Hell, it could be fixed just by expansion — adding on the CI's POV, possibly a third version telling other version of what happened. (Yeah right it was unprecedented as a betrayal. Yeah right the O5s were stunned when they really defected. Yeah right they had nothing to do with it. That kind of thing.)

For now, it's a neutral vote.
